title: ついでに — “while at it / on the same occasion”
summary: Verb dictionary / ta-form, or noun の + ついでに means “taking the opportunity of doing ～, I also do another thing.” The main action is the first one, and the second action is a small extra done at the same time and place.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形／た形 ＋ ついでに
patterns.gloss: dictionary / ta-form + ついでに (行くついでに, 行ったついでに)

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ の ＋ ついでに
patterns.gloss: noun + の + ついでに (買い物のついでに)

body.p: The first part is the main errand and the second part is something small done on the occasion. 買い物のついでに、郵便局にも寄った. A noun takes の. Both ordinary actions and movements work: 散歩のついでに.
The dictionary form means the action is not finished yet (行くついでに), and the ta-form means it has been done (行ったついでに). Either can be used.
The second action must be convenient and minor. It is not used for something that takes great effort. It is also rude to say it about doing a favor for someone to their face.

examples.ja: 買（か）い物（もの）のついでに、郵便局（ゆうびんきょく）にも寄（よ）った。
examples.romaji: Kaimono no tsuide ni, yūbinkyoku ni mo yotta.
examples.tr: While out shopping, I also stopped by the post office.

examples.ja: 散歩（さんぽ）のついでに、パンを買（か）ってきた。
examples.romaji: Sanpo no tsuide ni, pan o katte kita.
examples.tr: While I was out on a walk, I bought some bread.

examples.ja: 出張（しゅっちょう）のついでに、昔（むかし）の友（とも）だちに会（あ）った。
examples.romaji: Shutchō no tsuide ni, mukashi no tomodachi ni atta.
examples.tr: While on a business trip, I met up with an old friend.

pitfalls: With a noun, don't forget の: 買い物のついでに.
The second action should be small. Do not use it for the main purpose of the trip.
